transcript.speaker: Grandmother
transcript.words: Otto, you were meant to clear the path. Not bring it in. Breakfast is waiting.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: Morning, Grandmother.

transcript.speaker: Grandmother
transcript.words: Bruno. Your wife's waiting in the breakfast room.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: Is Sadie still angry?

transcript.speaker: Sadie
transcript.words: You came home after midnight.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: I went for a walk.

transcript.speaker: Sadie
transcript.words: Then why do you smell like parmesan? And rosemary?

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: Sadie.

transcript.speaker: Sadie
transcript.words: Bella.

transcript.speaker: Sadie
transcript.words: Your ex.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: She offered me a snack.

transcript.speaker: Sadie
transcript.words: And you stayed until midnight?

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: It was very good cheese.

transcript.speaker: Penny
transcript.words: Dad, are you in trouble?

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: Your mother and I are discussing breakfast.

transcript.speaker: Sadie
transcript.words: Penny, your father is changing the subject.

transcript.speaker: Penny
transcript.words: Then can I have his cheese?

transcript.speaker: Sadie
transcript.words: Yes. He's had quite enough.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: Grandmother? Come back in. Penny's negotiating for your breakfast.

transcript.speaker: Grandmother
transcript.words: Your brother Sebastian did that too. He'd steal breakfast without leaving his bed.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: My twin got the looks, I got the sausage.

transcript.speaker: Grandmother
transcript.words: You were supposed to share it.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: We did. Then the kennel burned down. They never found him. He's dead, Grandmother. You can't spend every morning waiting.

transcript.speaker: Grandmother
transcript.words: You're allowed to miss him, Bruno.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: I do. That's why I can't keep looking at that.

transcript.speaker: Grandmother
transcript.words: Wait. That smell. From the grooming room.

transcript.speaker: Grandmother
transcript.words: He used to hide in here. As if I couldn't smell him. Fresh fur. No, I'm imagining it. Bruno. Come and smell this.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: We heard you. What's happened?

transcript.speaker: Grandmother
transcript.words: This smells like Sebastian.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: We all shed, Grandmother. It's probably mine.

transcript.speaker: Grandmother
transcript.words: I thought that too. Then I smelled it again.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: You really think he's been here?

transcript.speaker: Grandmother
transcript.words: I don't know. I need you to look.

transcript.speaker: Bruno
transcript.words: I wish it were him. I do. But nobody survived that fire.

transcript.speaker: Grandmother
transcript.words: Then whose scent is this?

transcript.words: BENEATH THE DOUBLE COAT: The Secret in the Snow

audience.retelling: Talking dogs discuss breakfast and infidelity before a grandmother dog discovers fresh fur that smells like her allegedly dead grandson.

understood.claim: Bruno is married to Sadie and they have a puppy.

uncertainties.question: Is the dog in the barn at the end Sebastian?

The grandmother follows a scent to the grooming room.
Bruno and Sadie respond to the grandmother calling.
Sebastian is established as dead before the scent is found.
